questions.question: "Rajendra I" was the son of which chola ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajaraja I**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Rajendra I**, one of the most prominent rulers of the Chola dynasty, was the son of **Rajaraja I**, the great Chola emperor who laid the foundation for the Chola Empire’s expansion and administrative reforms. 
• **Rajaraja I** ruled from **985–1014 CE** and is credited with consolidating and strengthening the Chola dynasty into a formidable empire. 
• Under Rajaraja I’s reign, the Chola Empire witnessed significant territorial expansion, including conquests in Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and parts of South India, which Rajendra I later expanded further. 
• Rajaraja I was instrumental in initiating large-scale temple constructions, including the renowned **Brihadeeswarar Temple** at Thanjavur, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. His architectural patronage was a legacy continued by his son, Rajendra I. 
• Rajendra I succeeded his father in **1014 CE** and carried forward his legacy by further expanding the empire to include regions like Southeast Asia and the Gangetic plains. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Rajaraja I’s Achievements:** 
• He established a highly organized and efficient administrative system, dividing the empire into provinces called **mandalams** for better governance. 
• He introduced a systematic revenue collection system and ensured the prosperity of the empire through trade and agriculture. 
• Rajaraja I’s military campaigns led to the annexation of northern Sri Lanka, which he renamed **Mummudi Chola Mandalam**. 
• He was a patron of art and architecture and played a significant role in the development of Dravidian temple architecture. 
• **Rajendra I’s Contributions:** 
• Rajendra I is known for his naval expeditions, particularly the conquest of the **Srivijaya Empire** (modern-day Indonesia and Malaysia), marking the Chola Empire as a maritime power. 
• He built a new capital city called **Gangaikonda Cholapuram** to commemorate his victory over the Ganga dynasty. 
• Under his reign, the Chola Empire became one of the most powerful empires in Asia, with influence spreading across Southeast Asia. 
• Rajendra I also constructed numerous temples and irrigation systems, further strengthening the empire’s infrastructure. 
• **Other Options Explained:** 
• **Vijayalaya:** He was the founder of the Chola dynasty in the 9th century CE, but he was not the father of Rajendra I. 
• **Parantaka Chola I:** He was an earlier ruler of the Chola dynasty (907–950 CE) and a significant figure in its early expansion but not directly related to Rajendra I. 
• **Kulothunga:** He was a later Chola ruler who reigned in the 11th century CE, long after Rajendra I’s time. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Brihadeeswarar Temple:** Built by Rajaraja I, this temple remains a masterpiece of Chola architecture and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. 
• **Chola Navy:** The Chola dynasty developed one of the most powerful navies in ancient India, which played a crucial role in their conquests under Rajendra I. 
• **Trade and Economy:** Both Rajaraja I and Rajendra I encouraged maritime trade, especially in the Indian Ocean region, fostering economic prosperity. 
• **Inscriptional Evidence:** The reigns of Rajaraja I and Rajendra I are well-documented through inscriptions, which provide valuable insights into their governance and achievements. 
2f:T269e,

questions.question: As of 31 st July 2025 , United Nations Security Council has how many members including permanent and non-permanent members?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **United Nations Security Council (UNSC)** is one of the six principal organs of the **United Nations (UN)** and is responsible for maintaining international peace and security.

• As of **31st July 2025**, the UNSC comprises a total of **15 members**, which include both permanent and non-permanent members.

• The UNSC has **5 permanent members** with veto power: **China**, **France**, **Russia**, **United Kingdom**, and **United States**.

• The remaining **10 non-permanent members** are elected for a **two-year term** by the United Nations General Assembly, with seats allocated based on geographical representation.

• The non-permanent members represent regions such as **Asia-Pacific**, **Africa**, **Latin America**, **Eastern Europe**, and **Western Europe**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Permanent Members and Veto Power:**

• The **5 permanent members** are often referred to as the **P5** or **Permanent Five**.

• Each permanent member has the power to **veto any substantive resolution**, effectively blocking its adoption.

• This veto power is a significant feature of the UNSC and has often been a subject of debate regarding fairness and reform.

• **Non-Permanent Members:**

• The **10 non-permanent members** are elected by the **United Nations General Assembly** for a **two-year term**.

• They are chosen to ensure equitable geographical representation, with specific numbers of seats allocated to different regions.

• For example, **3 seats** are allocated to Africa, **2 to Asia-Pacific**, **2 to Latin America and the Caribbean**, **1 to Eastern Europe**, and **2 to Western Europe and others**.

• **Functions of the UNSC:**

• The UNSC has the primary responsibility for the **maintenance of international peace and security**.

• It can authorize the deployment of peacekeeping forces, impose sanctions, and approve military action to address threats to peace.

• The council also recommends the appointment of the **UN Secretary-General** and the admission of new members to the UN.

• **Reforms and Criticism:**

• The structure and functioning of the UNSC have been criticized for being **outdated and unrepresentative**, particularly with regard to the permanent membership.

• There have been calls for reforms, such as expanding the number of permanent members to include countries like **India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan** (often collectively referred to as the G4 nations).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Historical Background:**

• The UNSC was established in **1945** following the conclusion of **World War II** as part of the United Nations.

• It replaced the **League of Nations**, which had failed to prevent global conflict.

• **Voting System:**

• For a resolution to pass, it requires the affirmative votes of **9 out of 15 members**, including the consent of all **5 permanent members**.

• If any permanent member casts a veto, the resolution cannot be adopted.

• **Peacekeeping Operations:**

• The UNSC plays a critical role in authorizing and overseeing **peacekeeping missions** across the globe.

• These missions are conducted in conflict zones to **maintain ceasefires**, protect civilians, and support political processes.

</ul

questions.question: Who took charge as the Director General of the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) in September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrit Mohan Prasad**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Amrit Mohan Prasad** was appointed as the **Director General** of the **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)** in **September 2024**. 
• The **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)** is one of the **Central Armed Police Forces** (CAPF) of India, responsible for guarding the borders of India with **Nepal** and **Bhutan**. 
• Amrit Mohan Prasad is a distinguished officer with extensive experience in the field of law enforcement and border security. 
• He succeeds the outgoing Director General and has been tasked with ensuring the **effective functioning of the SSB** and maintaining the security of India’s borders. 
• The appointment of the Director General of SSB is a significant decision as it directly impacts the operational efficiency and strategic planning of India’s border security system. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB):** 
• The **SSB** was established in **1963** in the wake of the **Chinese aggression** and was initially tasked with fostering a sense of security among the people living in border areas. 
• It operates under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, Government of India. 
• The SSB’s primary duties include **border guarding**, **counter-insurgency operations**, and **providing assistance during natural disasters**. 
• **Role of the Director General:** 
• The Director General (DG) is the **highest-ranking official** in the SSB and oversees all operations, planning, and administration. 
• The DG is responsible for implementing government policies and ensuring the operational preparedness of the force. 
• **Other Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF):** 
• In addition to the SSB, India has several other CAPFs, including the **Border Security Force (BSF)**, **Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)**, **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)**, and **Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)**. 
• Each of these forces is tasked with specific responsibilities, ranging from border security to industrial safety and counter-terrorism. 
• **Key Challenges Faced by SSB:** 
• Securing borders with **porous boundaries** shared with Nepal and Bhutan. 
• Combating **illegal immigration**, **smuggling**, and **human trafficking** across the borders. 
• Maintaining peace and order in sensitive border regions and fostering **community development programs**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The Director General of SSB is generally appointed from the **Indian Police Service (IPS)**, ensuring that the officer has extensive knowledge and experience in law enforcement and border management. 
• The SSB also plays a vital role in **humanitarian efforts** during natural disasters and emergencies in border regions. 
• India’s **border security strategy** is continuously evolving, with a focus on adopting modern technology and improving infrastructure in border areas. 
• Effective leadership in the SSB is crucial to maintaining the **integrity of India’s borders** and ensuring the safety of border communities.

questions.question: Finance Minister during her budget speech 2025-26 has announced extension of Jal Jeevan Mission until _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2028**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Jal Jeevan Mission** was launched by the Government of India in **2019** under the Ministry of Jal Shakti to provide **functional tap water connections** to every rural household. 
• The scheme's primary goal is to ensure **safe and adequate drinking water** for all rural homes through individual household tap connections by **2024**. 
• During the **Union Budget 2025-26**, the **Finance Minister** announced the extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission until **2028**. This decision is intended to address the challenges and ensure the scheme's comprehensive success. 
• The extension aims to cover any remaining gaps in rural areas and enhance the sustainability of water supply systems. 
• This extended timeline reflects the government's commitment to achieving **universal access to clean drinking water** in rural areas while addressing infrastructure and resource challenges. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission Objectives:** 
• To provide **adequate and safe drinking water** to every household in rural areas through tap connections. 
• To promote the judicious use of water and enhance the **sustainability of water resources**. 
• To ensure the functioning and maintenance of water supply systems through **community participation**. 
• **Key Features of Jal Jeevan Mission:** 
• Focus on **source sustainability** measures such as recharge and reuse through greywater management. 
• Emphasis on the convergence of other schemes like **MGNREGA** and **Swachh Bharat Mission** to create water resource structures. 
• Capacity building and training for village-level institutions to manage water supply infrastructure. 
• **Budget Allocation:** 
• The Government of India allocated **Rs. 60,000 crore** for the Jal Jeevan Mission in the 2023-24 budget. 
• This reflects the government's prioritization of **water security** and rural development. 
• **Achievements So Far:** 
• As of **2023**, over **11 crore rural households** have been provided with tap water connections under the Jal Jeevan Mission. 
• Several states, such as **Goa, Telangana, and Haryana**, have achieved 100% coverage. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Challenges in Implementation:** 
• Ensuring water availability in **water-stressed areas** and regions with limited resources. 
• Addressing issues of **quality** such as contamination by fluoride, arsenic, and other pollutants. 
• Promoting **community ownership** and participation for the sustainable operation of water systems. 
• **Global Perspective:** 
• The Jal Jeevan Mission aligns with the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 6**, which aims to ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all. 
• Similar initiatives like the **Safe Water Network** and **Water.org** work towards clean water access globally. </ul

questions.question: District Project Management Units (DPMUs) initiative launched under PM Vishwakarma scheme in July 2025 comes under which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **District Project Management Units (DPMUs)** initiative under the **PM Vishwakarma Scheme** was launched in July 2025 to empower artisans and craftsmen across India.
 
• This scheme is implemented by the **Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)**, which is responsible for promoting, developing, and enhancing the skills of small and medium-scale entrepreneurs in India.
 
• The **PM Vishwakarma Scheme** aims to support traditional artisans and craftsmen such as carpenters, blacksmiths, potters, and cobblers, among others, to enhance their productivity and improve their livelihoods.
 
• Under this initiative, **DPMUs** act as implementation units at the district level, ensuring effective delivery of scheme benefits, including skill training, financial support, and market linkages for artisans.
 
• The Ministry of MSME plays a crucial role in achieving the objectives of this scheme by coordinating with state governments and local bodies to address the challenges faced by artisans and small-scale entrepreneurs.

questions.question: Which of the following sports was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basketball**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Basketball** was invented by **Dr. James Naismith** in **1891**. It was originally designed as an indoor sport to keep athletes active during the winter months.
 
• Naismith, a Canadian-American physical educator, created the game while working at the **International YMCA Training School** in Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.
 
• The original game consisted of throwing a soccer ball into a peach basket that was nailed to a balcony, hence the name "Basketball."
 
• The first game of basketball was played on **December 21, 1891**, with **13 basic rules** that Naismith had formulated.
 
• Over time, the sport evolved, leading to the development of modern rules, professional leagues like the **NBA (National Basketball Association)**, and widespread global popularity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dr. James Naismith:**

 
 
• Born on **November 6, 1861**, in Almonte, Ontario, Canada.
 
• He was a physician, teacher, and coach with a deep interest in physical education.
 
• In addition to inventing basketball, Naismith also introduced the first football helmet.
 
 
 
• **Development of Basketball:**
 
 
• The first professional basketball league, the **National Basketball League (NBL)**, was established in **1898**.
 
• The **NBA** was formed in **1949** after a merger between the NBL and the Basketball Association of America (BAA).
 
• Basketball became an **Olympic sport** in **1936**, with the first Olympic event held in Berlin, Germany.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Sports:**
 
 
• **Cricket:** Originated in England during the 16th century and is widely popular in countries like India, Australia, and England.
 
• **Hockey:** The modern version of field hockey originated in England in the mid-19th century and is the national sport of India and Pakistan.
 
• **Polo:** A sport with ancient roots, played on horseback, originating in Persia (modern-day Iran) as early as the 6th century BCE.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Basketball:**
 
 
• It is one of the most popular sports globally, with millions of fans and players across continents.
 
• The sport promotes physical fitness, teamwork, strategic thinking, and social interaction.
 
• Key tournaments include the **NBA Finals**, **FIBA World Cup**, and **Olympic Games**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Reach:** Basketball is played in over **200 countries**, and its governing body, **FIBA (International Basketball Federation)**, oversees global regulations and competitions.
 
• **NBA Stars:** Legendary players like **Michael Jordan**, **LeBron James**, and **Kobe Bryant** have contributed to the sport's immense popularity.
 
• **Women's Basketball:** The **WNBA** (Women's National Basketball Association) was founded in **1996** and has been a platform for female athletes to showcase their talents.
 
• **Paralympics:** Basketball is also a popular sport in the **Paralympic Games**, played as **wheelchair basketball**.

questions.question: The game of judo was invented in the year ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The game of judo was invented in the year 1882.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Judo** is a modern martial art created by **Dr. Jigoro Kano** in the year **1882** in Japan. 
• The term "Judo" translates to **"The Gentle Way"** in English, emphasizing the art's focus on skill and technique rather than brute force. 
• Dr. Jigoro Kano founded the **Kodokan Judo Institute** in Tokyo, Japan, to teach and promote Judo as both a sport and a way of life. 
• Judo was developed as a refinement of **traditional Japanese jujutsu** techniques, focusing on throws, grapples, and submissions. 
• It became an **Olympic sport** in **1964**, debuting at the Tokyo Summer Olympics, further solidifying its global popularity. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Development of Judo:** 
• **Dr. Jigoro Kano**, born in 1860, was an educator and athlete who sought to modernize martial arts by creating a discipline that combined physical education, mental discipline, and moral education. 
• Judo prioritizes techniques such as **throws (nage-waza)**, **pins (osaekomi-waza)**, and **submission techniques (shime-waza and kansetsu-waza)**. 
• Unlike many martial arts, Judo avoids strikes and weapon techniques, focusing on unarmed combat and using an opponent's strength against them. 
• **Global Popularity:** 
• Judo is now practiced worldwide, with millions of practitioners across various countries. 
• The International Judo Federation (IJF), founded in **1951**, oversees competitive Judo globally, organizing events such as the World Judo Championships. 
• Judo's inclusion in the Olympics in **1964** marked a turning point in its international recognition and popularity. 
• **Philosophy and Values:** 
• Judo promotes the principles of **mutual welfare and benefit**, along with **maximum efficiency** in the use of energy. 
• It emphasizes respect, discipline, and personal growth, aligning with its roots in traditional Japanese culture. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• Judo evolved from **jujutsu**, which was practiced by Japanese samurai as a means of self-defense. 
• Dr. Kano refined jujutsu techniques to create Judo, removing dangerous and outdated methods to ensure safety and accessibility for practitioners. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Modern Judo Competitions:** 
• Judo matches are conducted on a mat called a **tatami**, where competitors aim to score points through throws, pins, and submissions. 
• Scoring in Judo includes **Ippon (full point)**, **Waza-ari (half point)**, and **Yuko (minor score)**, with Ippon being the ultimate goal for victory. 
• Weight classes ensure fair competition among participants, making Judo accessible to individuals of different body types. 
• **Educational Impact:** 
• Judo is widely taught in schools and universities, especially in Japan, as a means of physical education and moral development. 
• It is recognized as a way to improve physical fitness, mental resilience, and social values. 
• **Judo Uniform:** 
• Practitioners wear a uniform called a **judogi**, consisting of a jacket, pants, and a belt that signifies rank and skill level. 
• Belt colors range from white (beginner) to black (advanced), with additional ranks such as dan levels for experienced practitioners. </ul

questions.question: 'Mando' is a slow verse and refrain composition dealing with love, tragedy and both social injustice and political resistance. It is related to which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Mando** is a traditional Goan form of lyrical music and dance that expresses themes of **love, tragedy, social injustice, and political resistance**. It is an integral part of Goan culture. 
• The origins of Mando can be traced back to the 19th century, during the Portuguese colonial period in Goa. It combines Indian and Western musical elements, reflecting the cultural fusion of the time. 
• Mando songs are typically slow and melodious, with verses and refrains. They are performed with an ensemble of musical instruments such as the **violin, guitar, and Ghumat** (a traditional Goan percussion instrument). 
• The dance associated with Mando is graceful and elegant, often performed by couples dressed in traditional Goan attire. It showcases the rich heritage of Goa. 
• Mando serves as a medium to highlight the **socio-political struggles** of Goans during colonial rule, making it not just an art form but also a historical narrative. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Characteristics of Mando Music:** 
• Mando songs are typically written in the **Konkani language**, the official language of Goa. 
• The themes of Mando often reflect the **emotions of love, heartbreak, and longing**, as well as the social issues faced by Goan society. 
• The music is slow-paced, with a melancholic tone that evokes deep emotional responses. 
• Traditional instruments like the **violin, guitar, and percussion** are used to create a harmonious blend of melodies. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The Mando evolved during the Portuguese rule in Goa, combining Indian and European musical traditions. The colonial influence is evident in the use of Western instruments. 
• It was popularized among the Goan elite as a form of artistic expression and gradually spread to the masses. 
• During the freedom struggle and social movements, Mando songs were used to express **political resistance** and critique social injustices. 
• **Other Cultural Forms of Goa:** 
• Goa is known for its vibrant cultural heritage, including forms like **Dekhni**, **Fugdi**, and **Dashavatar**. 
• The **Dekhni dance** represents a blend of Western and Indian music, performed during festive occasions. 
• **Fugdi** is a folk dance performed primarily by women during religious and social celebrations. 
• **Dashavatar** is a theatrical performance depicting the ten incarnations of Lord Vishnu, showcasing Goa's deep spiritual traditions. 
• **Other States Mentioned:** 
• **Uttarakhand:** Known for its folk music like Jagar and Pandav Nritya, which are rooted in spiritual and mythological themes. 
• **Bihar:** Famous for Bhojpuri folk music and dances like Jat-Jatin and Sohar, which depict rural life and culture. 
• **Tamil Nadu:** Renowned for classical music and dance forms like Bharatanatyam and Carnatic music, which have ancient origins.

questions.question: What is the term used to describe how the brain interprets the frequency of an emitted sound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pitch**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Pitch** is the perceptual property of sound that allows the brain to interpret the **frequency** of an emitted sound. 
• It is closely related to the **frequency of vibration**. Higher frequencies are perceived as higher pitch, while lower frequencies are perceived as lower pitch. 
• Pitch is a **subjective sensation**, meaning it is how humans perceive sounds rather than an objective, measurable property of the sound wave itself. 
• For example, a musical note produced by a tuning fork vibrating at **440 Hz** is perceived as the pitch "A" in musical terms. 
• This term is distinct from related terms like **tone** (refers to sound quality), **frequency** (a measurable property of sound waves), and **wavelength** (the spatial property of sound waves). 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Frequency**: 
• It is the number of sound wave cycles that occur in one second, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**. 
• Humans generally hear frequencies ranging from **20 Hz** to **20,000 Hz**. 
• Frequency is an objective, measurable property of sound waves. 
• **Tone**: 
• It refers to the quality or character of sound, often determined by the sound's frequency and amplitude. 
• Musical tones, for instance, are characterized by a specific pitch, timbre, and duration. 
• **Wavelength**: 
• It is the physical distance between two consecutive peaks or troughs of a sound wave. 
• Wavelength is inversely proportional to frequency: higher frequency means shorter wavelength. 
• It is typically measured in meters (m). 
• **Applications of Pitch**: 
• In **music**, pitch helps differentiate musical notes and create harmony. 
• In **speech**, pitch variations convey emotions, questions, and emphasis. 
• It is also used in **sonar technology** and tuning musical instruments. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Distinction Between Related Terms:** 
• **Pitch**: A perceptual property that depends on frequency. 
• **Frequency**: A measurable property of the number of sound wave cycles per second. 
• **Wavelength**: The spatial distance between cycles of sound waves. 
• **Tone**: Refers to the quality or richness of sound. 
• **Biological Basis of Pitch Perception:** 
• The human ear perceives pitch via hair cells in the cochlea of the inner ear. 
• Specific regions of the cochlea are sensitive to different frequencies, a property known as **tonotopic organization**. </ul

questions.question: As per the Industrial policy resolution 1956 of India, industries were divided into how many category?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956** was a landmark policy document that shaped India's industrial development post-independence.
 
• As per this policy, industries were classified into **three categories**, depending on the degree of state control and participation:
 
 
• **Category A:** Industries exclusively under the state’s domain, such as defense, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• **Category B:** Industries where private enterprises could operate, but the state would progressively participate, such as chemicals, fertilizers, and road transport.
 
• **Category C:** All other industries that were left to private enterprise but still subject to state regulations and policies.
 
 
 
• The classification aimed to ensure a **mixed economy model** where both public and private sectors contributed to national development.
 
• It emphasized **state-led industrialization**, focusing on heavy industries and infrastructure to reduce dependency on foreign imports.
 
• This resolution was influenced by the **Soviet model of economic planning** and marked a significant step in implementing the vision of a socialist pattern of society in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956:**

 
 
• To promote a **socialist pattern of society** by reducing income inequalities and wealth concentration.
 
• To achieve a **self-reliant economy** by focusing on heavy industries and infrastructure development.
 
• To support the growth of **small-scale industries** for employment generation and equitable distribution of resources.
 
• To ensure the **balanced regional development** by setting up industries in less developed areas.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956:**
 
 
• It laid the foundation for the **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** in India.
 
• The focus on heavy industries led to the establishment of **steel plants, power projects, and machine-building industries**.
 
• It facilitated the **growth of the mixed economy**, combining public and private sector roles in industrial development.
 
 
 
• **Relation to Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 was implemented during the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)**, which emphasized heavy industries and a state-led development approach.
 
• The plan was designed by the renowned economist **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948:**
 
 
• The **1948 resolution** was more general and aimed at promoting industrial growth post-independence.
 
• The **1956 resolution** was more specific and focused on achieving a **socialist economy** by clearly defining the role of state and private sectors in industrialization.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 identified **17 industries exclusively reserved for the state** under Category A.
 
• Category B included industries where both public and private sectors could coexist, with a focus on eventual state control.
 
• It played a significant role in promoting **import substitution** to reduce dependency on foreign goods.
 
• The resolution is considered a cornerstone of India's **economic and industrial policies** in the post-independence era.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a reason of Brain drain in India?

I. Low job opportunities in India

II. Low quality of higher education in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Low job opportunities in India:** 
• The lack of sufficient and suitable employment opportunities in India has been a major cause of **brain drain**. 
• Many skilled and educated individuals move abroad in search of better-paying jobs, enhanced career growth, and improved working conditions. 
• The unemployment rate in India, which has fluctuated over the years, often contributes to individuals choosing to migrate. *Hence, statement I is correct.* 
• **Low quality of higher education in India:** 
• Although India has numerous educational institutions, the **quality of higher education** often fails to meet global standards. 
• Factors such as outdated curricula, limited research opportunities, and insufficient infrastructure drive students to pursue education in developed countries offering cutting-edge facilities. 
• India ranks lower in global university rankings, which influences students' decisions to study abroad. *Hence, statement II is correct.* 
• **Combined impact of both factors:** 
• The combination of inadequate job opportunities and the substandard quality of higher education creates a strong push factor for migration. 
• Countries with better opportunities and higher-quality education attract Indian talent, leading to a continuous brain drain. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Brain Drain:** 
• **Definition:** Brain drain refers to the emigration of highly skilled and educated individuals from their home country to another nation for better opportunities. 
• **Major destinations:** Countries like the **United States, Canada, Australia, and the United Kingdom** are popular destinations for Indian migrants due to their better job markets and education systems. 
• **Impact on India:** Brain drain negatively affects India's economic growth as it leads to a loss of skilled workforce required for innovation and development. 
• **Government Initiatives to curb brain drain:** 
• The Indian government has launched programs like **Skill India Mission** and **Startup India** to encourage entrepreneurship and create more job opportunities. 
• Efforts are being made to improve the quality of higher education by establishing world-class universities and increasing funding for research. 
• **Statistical Data:** 
• According to the **United Nations**, India has one of the largest diasporas globally, with over **18 million people** living outside the country (2020 data). 
• In 2021, nearly **1 lakh Indian students** migrated to foreign countries for higher education, highlighting the extent of brain drain. 
• **Reasons for global preference:** 
• Developed nations offer better infrastructure, higher salaries, and advanced research opportunities. 
• Scholarships and financial aid provided by foreign universities attract students from developing countries like India. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Role of Education Rankings:** Indian universities often fail to secure top positions in **QS World Rankings** or **Times Higher Education Rankings**, influencing students to opt for foreign institutions. 
• **Economic factors:** The disparity in salaries between India and developed countries contributes significantly to brain drain. 
• **Reverse Brain Drain:** Some initiatives like **Make in India** aim to attract skilled professionals back to India by creating favorable conditions for their return. 
• **Technological advancements:** Developed countries often provide access to cutting-edge technologies, which is a major pull factor for skilled professionals. </ul

questions.question: In the context of economy, which of the following is an example of Intermediate good?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper used for making utensils**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Intermediate goods** are goods that are used as inputs in the production of other goods and services. They are not the final products consumed by end users. 
• **Copper used for making utensils** is considered an intermediate good because it is used as a raw material in the production process to create finished goods such as utensils. 
• Unlike final goods, intermediate goods are not directly purchased for consumption; they undergo further processing or transformation in industries. 
• Examples of intermediate goods include **steel** used for manufacturing cars, **flour** used for baking bread, and **wood** used in furniture production. 
• Other options such as a **shirt**, **television purchased by households**, and **refrigerators** are considered final goods because they are consumed directly by individuals and are not used as inputs for further production. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Final Goods vs Intermediate Goods:** 
• Final goods are products consumed directly by households or businesses, providing utility without further processing. Examples include **appliances, clothing, and food items**. 
• Intermediate goods, in contrast, are used in the production process to create final goods. They are not consumed directly and include items such as **raw materials**, **components**, and **semi-finished products**. 
• **Characteristics of Intermediate Goods:** 
• They are used as **inputs** in the production process. 
• They are not intended for final consumption. 
• Examples include **chemicals** for manufacturing, **glass** for windows, and **copper** for utensils. 
• **Role in the Economy:** 
• Intermediate goods are crucial for industries as they form the backbone of the production process. 
• Their demand is a key indicator of industrial activity and economic growth. 
• For instance, increased demand for **steel** suggests growth in construction and automobile industries. 
• **Examples of Intermediate Goods:** 
• **Textile fabric:** Used in the production of clothing. 
• **Plastic:** Used in the manufacturing of toys, electronics, and containers. 
• **Wood:** Used in furniture production. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Economic Impact:** 
• Intermediate goods are often traded internationally, influencing global trade dynamics. For example, **India exports steel** to other countries for industrial use. 
• They contribute significantly to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** as their production is included in the calculation of industrial output. 
• **Distinction in Accounting:** 
• Intermediate goods are excluded from the calculation of GDP to avoid **double counting**, as their value is already embedded in the final goods. 
• **Government Policies:** 
• Government often imposes taxes or provides subsidies on intermediate goods to regulate industrial production and costs. 
• For example, reducing import duties on **raw materials** can promote domestic manufacturing industries. </ul

 __ 
• Deoxygenated blood from various parts of the body returns to the heart through two large veins - the **superior vena cava** and the **inferior vena cava**. 
• The superior vena cava collects blood from the upper part of the body (head, neck, arms), while the inferior vena cava collects blood from the lower part of the body (abdomen, legs). 
• Both these veins empty deoxygenated blood into the **right atrium**, which is the first chamber of the heart to receive this blood. 
• From the right atrium, the blood is pushed into the **right ventricle** during atrial contraction. 
• The right atrium plays a crucial role in the circulation of blood as it acts as a receiving chamber for deoxygenated blood, initiating the pulmonary circulation process to re-oxygenate the blood. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Heart Chambers and Their Functions:** 
• The human heart has **four chambers**: the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle. 
• The **right atrium** receives deoxygenated blood from the body and pumps it into the right ventricle. 
• The **right ventricle** pumps the blood to the lungs for oxygenation through the pulmonary artery. 
• The **left atrium** receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and sends it to the left ventricle. 
• The **left ventricle** pumps the oxygenated blood to the entire body through the aorta. 
• **Pulmonary Circulation:** 
• Deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle to the lungs through the **pulmonary artery**. 
• In the lungs, carbon dioxide is exchanged for oxygen in the alveoli (tiny air sacs). 
• The oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium of the heart via the **pulmonary veins**. 
• **Systemic Circulation:** 
• Oxygenated blood is pumped from the left ventricle to the entire body through the **aorta**. 
• The body tissues utilize oxygen and nutrients from the blood, and in return, the blood picks up carbon dioxide and waste products. 
• Deoxygenated blood is then returned to the right atrium through the superior and inferior vena cavae. 
• **Valves of the Heart:** 
• The heart has four major valves to ensure the unidirectional flow of blood: **tricuspid valve, pulmonary valve, mitral valve, and aortic valve**. 
• The **tricuspid valve** is located between the right atrium and right ventricle, preventing backflow of blood. 
• The **pulmonary valve** lies between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery, regulating blood flow to the lungs. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The **right atrium** is part of the systemic circulation and acts as the entry point for blood returning from the body. 
• The separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in the heart's chambers is critical for efficient circulation in humans and other mammals. 
• The heart beats approximately **72 times per minute** on average, ensuring continuous circulation of blood. 
• Any obstruction in the flow of blood to or from the right atrium can lead to serious cardiovascular conditions, such as **right heart failure**. </ul

questions.question: Who among the following travelers visited India in the 7th century CE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• **Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)**, a Chinese traveler, visited India during the **7th century CE**. He is known for his detailed accounts of Indian society, culture, and religion during the reign of **Harsha (606–647 CE)**. 
• Xuanzang came to India primarily to study Buddhism and collect sacred Buddhist texts. He spent around **17 years** in India, traveling extensively across the subcontinent. 
• During his time in India, Xuanzang visited major Buddhist sites such as **Nalanda University, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, and Kushinagar**. He studied at Nalanda, one of the most prestigious learning centers of the time. 
• Xuanzang documented his journey in the text titled **"Great Tang Records on the Western Regions" (Da Tang Xi Yu Ji)**, which provides invaluable insights into the political, social, and religious conditions of 7th-century India. 
• He described the flourishing of Buddhism in India, the caste system, the structure of Indian cities, and the administration under Emperor Harsha, making his records a significant historical source for understand
